tools.name: publish
tools.description:
Publish files as a live website on Flowershow and get a shareable URL. Use when the user says "publish this", "put this online", "make this a website", "share this as a page" or "host this".

Accepts Markdown (.md, rendered as a styled page with navigation), HTML (.html, served as-is), Word document

tools.name: list-sites
tools.description: List the sites in the signed-in Flowershow account and sites shared with it (role editor), with their siteId (use it with list-files to see what a site has, and with publish to update it), URL and when each was last published. If the user is not signed in yet, calling it asks them to sign in to Flow

tools.name: list-files
tools.description: List the files currently on one of the signed-in user's Flowershow sites: each path, its size in bytes and when it last changed. Use it before updating a site in a new conversation, to see which pages exist, pick the right paths to update or delete, and avoid duplicating a page under a new name. Get

tools.name: read-file
tools.description: Get the current text of one file on one of the signed-in user's Flowershow sites, e.g. index.md. Use it before changing a page that is already on the site, then publish the whole updated file, so the parts you didn't mean to change stay as they are. Text files only (Markdown, HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, ..

tools.name: claim-site
tools.description: Move an anonymous site published earlier in this conversation into the signed-in user's Flowershow account, so it no longer expires and can be updated with publish using siteId alone. Use when the user wants to keep a site that was published without an account. Needs the siteId and claimToken return

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "publish" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Publish files as a live website on Flowershow and get a shareable URL. Use when the user says "publish this", "put this online", "make this a website", "share t…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "publish" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: publish, list-sites, read-file · Private data: publish, list-sites, list-files, read-file · Public sink: publish, list-sites, read-file, claim-site · Destructive: publish, list-files.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: publish, list-sites, read-file · Private data: publish, list-sites, list-files, read-file · Public sink: publish, list-sites, read-file, claim-site · Destructive: publish, list-files

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "publish" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
